newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong overnight interbank rate up slightly.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong overnight interbank rate up slightly.

text.p: Hong Kong interbank market rates rose slightly on Thursday on month-end activity and demand for shorter-term money, dealers said.
Overnight money ended at 5-9/16 1/2 percent versus 5-3/16 percent at Wednesday midday while three-month finished unchanged at 5-1/2 percent, dealers said.
"There was some month-end demand, and also with four IPOs (initial public offerings) tomorrow, there is more demand for short-term money," a dealer with a foreign bank said.
Hong Kong government paper held mostly steady.
Yields for the seven-year Exchange Fund note ended unchanged at 7.11 percent, while the five-year remained at 6.76 percent.
Three-year notes yielded 6.18 percent versus 6.16 percent on Wednesday and the one-week bill yield rose to 4.93 percent versus 4.88 percent.
